questions.q: When is a row-level formula evaluated, relative to grouping and summarizing?
options: After the report is grouped and summarized
For each individual record, before grouping and summarizing
Only when the report is exported
At the same moment as the grand total
questions.explain: Row-level formulas are computed per record first. The report then filters, groups, and summarizes, and summary formulas run last on the totals.

questions.q: You need weighted pipeline: each opportunity's Amount times its Probability, then summed by owner. What is the correct approach?
options: A summary formula multiplying Sum of Amount by Sum of Probability
A cross filter on Probability
A row-level formula for Amount * Probability, then summarize it with Sum grouped by owner
A bucket column on Amount
questions.explain: The multiplication must happen per record before summing. Multiplying two already-summed columns gives a different, incorrect result.

questions.q: Which SQL construct is closest to a row-level formula?
options: A computed column or CASE expression in the SELECT list
A HAVING clause
A GROUP BY clause
A UNION
questions.explain: A row-level formula behaves like an expression in the SELECT list evaluated for each row, such as Amount * Probability or a CASE expression.

questions.q: The same calculated expression keeps being rebuilt in many of your reports. What does the lesson suggest?
options: Add more row-level formulas to each report
Move the logic into a joined report
Copy the report format to a new folder
Ask an admin to create a formula field on the object
questions.explain: A formula field lives in org metadata and is available in every report, list view, and query. Row-level formulas live only inside one report.

questions.q: What is a fair caution about row-level formulas in this lesson?
options: A report allows only a small number of them, so check current limits before designing around many
They cannot use any functions
They can only be used by system administrators
They permanently modify the underlying records
questions.explain: Salesforce caps how many row-level formulas a report can contain and supports different functions than summary formulas. They only affect the report, never the underlying data.
